lessons.title: Non-Fiction: What Is a Habitat?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about habitats from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about a habitat.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about habitats.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions about habitats.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about a habitat at home.

lessons.title: Multiplication as Equal Groups: Habitat Creatures
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent multiplication as equal groups.
success_criteria: I can show multiplication as equal groups.
I can write the multiplication sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model representing multiplication as equal groups (e.g. 3 groups of 4 woodlice).
lessons.independent_task: Children represent multiplication problems as equal groups using habitat-creature counters.
key_questions: How many groups? How many in each group?

differentiation.greater_depth: Use groups of 2, 5 and 10 and write matching sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Record multiplication as repeated groups understanding — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Find equal groups of objects at home and multiply.

lessons.title: What Is a Habitat?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a habitat provides for living things.
success_criteria: I can define a habitat.
I can say what it provides.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap basic needs of living things from Week 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the concept of habitat as a place providing what a living thing needs.
lessons.independent_task: Children match habitats to what they provide (shelter, food, water), recording their matching.
key_questions: Why is it suitable for this creature?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note habitat concept understanding — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Recap habitats and what they provide.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the habitat of a pet or animal you know.

lessons.title: Writing About a Habitat
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about a habitat.
success_criteria: I can describe a habitat.
I can use an expanded noun phrase.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about a habitat using an expanded noun phrase.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing a chosen habitat.
key_questions: What does this habitat look like?
Can you use an expanded noun phrase?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with varied noun phrases

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing and grammar application — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Describe a habitat to your family.

lessons.title: Division as Sharing: Habitat Creatures
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent division as sharing into equal groups.
success_criteria: I can share into equal groups.
I can write the division sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model representing division as sharing habitat-creature counters equally, writing division sentences.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve division problems by sharing, recording division sentences.
key_questions: How many each if shared equally?

differentiation.greater_depth: Share into groups of 2, 5 and 10 and write matching sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Record division as sharing understanding — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Practise sharing objects equally at home.

lessons.title: Habitats Around the School
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify habitats found around the school grounds.
success_criteria: I can identify a habitat outside.
I can name a creature that might live there.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap habitat types (pond, hedge, tree, grass).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss habitats likely found around the school (under logs, in hedges, in grass).
lessons.independent_task: Children explore the school grounds (or view photos) and record habitats found and creatures that might live there.

differentiation.greater_depth: Identify 5+ habitats and predict multiple creatures for each

lessons.assessment_notes: Note fieldwork/observation skill applied to habitats — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Look for a habitat in your garden or local park.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Habitat Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read habitat-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read habitat words.
I can read a sentence about habitats.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to habitat-themed words (e.g. 'pond', 'nest', 'burrow').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading habitat words over the week.

lessons.title: Measuring Habitat Temperatures
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare temperature using appropriate vocabulary in a habitat context.
success_criteria: I can say which habitat is warmer/cooler.
I can compare two habitat temperatures.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss which habitats might be warm/cool (pond vs sunny wall).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing temperature descriptions of different habitats.
lessons.independent_task: Children order habitat picture cards by likely temperature, recording reasoning.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note temperature comparison applied to a science context — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare the temperature of two places at home.

lessons.title: Habitats Around the World Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name habitats found around the world.
success_criteria: I can name a world habitat.
I can name a creature that lives there.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap world habitats from Year 1 (hot/cold places, under the sea).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate world habitat types (desert, ocean, rainforest, polar) and their creatures.
lessons.independent_task: Children match world habitats to their creatures, recording their matching.
resources_needed: World habitat and creature picture cards

differentiation.greater_depth: Match 6+ pairs and add a fact about each

lessons.assessment_notes: Note consolidation of Year 1 habitat learning, extended with Year 2 vocabulary — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Look up a world habitat together.

lessons.title: Habitat Riddles
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a habitat clearly enough for others to guess it.
success_criteria: I can give 3 clues about my habitat.
I can guess a friend's habitat.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models a riddle about a habitat.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how to give clear clues without naming the habitat.
lessons.independent_task: Children create and share habitat riddles in pairs, guessing each other's.

differentiation.support: Use picture cards to prompt clues

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive spoken language skill — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Share favourite riddles with the class.
lessons.home_link: Make up a habitat riddle for your family.

lessons.title: Habitat Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a habitat context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a habitat context (e.g. creatures found under logs).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve habitat-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a habitat word problem for your family.

lessons.title: What Would Happen If a Habitat Was Destroyed?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe why protecting habitats matters.
success_criteria: I can say what might happen if a habitat is destroyed.
I can name a way to protect habitats.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what happens if a pond dries up or a hedge is removed.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss simply and sensitively why habitat protection matters for creatures living there.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw a habitat and record one way to help protect it.
key_questions: What might happen without this habitat?
How could people help protect it?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain habitat loss reasoning in more detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early environmental awareness — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Talk about protecting a local habitat with your family.

lessons.title: Habitats Near Us Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about habitats.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about habitats, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why might a creature struggle without its habitat?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on habitat facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Multiplication and Division
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply multiplication and division skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can show multiplication as equal groups.
I can share into equal groups.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of multiplication and division as equal groups and sharing.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: multiplication, division.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 5 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising multiplication and division over the weekend.

lessons.title: Habitats Near Us Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about habitats near us and around the world.
success_criteria: I can name a local habitat and what lives there.
I can name a world habitat and what lives there.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering local and world habitats.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Habitats Near Us' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about habitats?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note habitat understanding progress, setting up microhabitats learning next week — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about habitats with your family.
